To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the selectivity of hidden units in AlexNet is overestimated by current measures, and that the most selective hidden layer units do not necessarily learn to represent the most salient features of the data.
\emph{Selectivity metrics can provide a misleading picture of unit selectivity, and that localist representations are not necessarily learned by NNs.}

1) The current measures of unit selectivity are problematic and can overestimate the degree of selectivity in units; and 2) Localist representations are learned more easily in RNNs than in CNNs because of the sequential nature of the input data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to best measure selectivity and interpretability, and how to understand the representations that are learned by different types of neural networks.

the question of how much of the information in a neural network is interpretable, and how to measure that information.

selectivity metrics are not a good measure of selectivity.
